dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_give_ref_lock_git_headroom` fail loudly (for example `if not hasattr(_ref_lock, "_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS"): raise pytest.UsageError(...)`) when the attribute it overrides is missing.
evidence: Removed in this diff: `monkeypatch.setattr(advisory_lock._load_ref_lock(), "_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS", 60.0)` and `monkeypatch.setattr(importlib.import_module("rebar.reconciler._ref_lock"), "_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS", 60.0)`. With its default raising=True, monkeypatch.setattr raises AttributeError when the target attribute does not exist.
src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock.py:44: _LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS = 5.0 (the name production code reads at call time)
dropped.finding: The session-wide headroom is a bare attribute assignment, so it no longer fails if `_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` is missing. The `monkeypatch.setattr` calls it replaces raised AttributeError in that case. If the production constant is renamed, this line just adds an unused module attribute. Every ref-lock test then quietly runs under the production bound again, and the only clue is an intermittent fail-closed flake on a busy host.
scenarios: A refactor renames `_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` (for example to `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECS`). The conftest assignment still succeeds, the headroom is gone, and the starved-host flakes (bugs ddc8, dissocial-malleable-tuna, c0ed) come back without any clear failure pointing at the conftest.
dropped.suggested_fix: Before assigning, check that the attribute exists: `if not hasattr(_ref_lock, "_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS"): raise pytest.UsageError("_ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS not found; update _give_ref_lock_git_headroom")`, then `_ref_lock._LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS = 60.0`.

dropped.finding: test_ref_backend_roundtrip_survives_a_slow_local_git_call has no check that its slow-git shim ran. This diff removes the fixture's own 60 s override, so the conftest headroom is now the only thing this test protects, and it is the only place this test is checked. But the test's assertions (a truthy oid, then read() is None) pass the same way whether or not the shim was used. If PATH lookup were bypassed (for example, git resolved to an absolute path or the env reset), the test would stay green and could not tell whether the headroom works. The new repair-pause test in this same diff adds exactly this liveness check.
scenarios: git is resolved to an absolute path or PATH is replaced in the subprocess env: the shim never runs, the test passes quickly, and it no longer shows that the headroom works for the advisory-lock path
